Gang culture weighs heavily on safety and control in prisons.
For example, prison gang activity leads to increases in offending in
prisons in the United States (e.g., Drury & DeLisi, 2011; Gaes et
al., 2002) and the United Kingdom (e.g., Wood, 2006; Wood &
Adler, 2001; Wood, Moir, & James, 2009; Wood, Williams, &
James, 2010). Research further shows that prison gangs severely
undermine the ability of prison staff to maintain a safe and orderly
environment (Griffin & Hepburn, 2006), leaving staff and prison-
ers believing that officials are not in full control of prisons (Wood,
2006; Wood & Adler, 2001). Consequently, if the negative influ-
ence of prison gang activities are to be reduced, there is a need to
identify which prisoners are most likely to become involved. The
